decision.title: The HTML, text, JSON and CSV methods; fn:serialize (packet )

body.p: . Every method runs on the 3.3 pipeline (); no second writer or escaper was added.

item.p: Escape styles: sxml_escape_style grows HTML, NONE (text), JSON and CSV; a method picks one in sxml_serializer_resolve_pipeline, so character maps, normalization, line endings and the encoding apply to all of them in one place. A new character context RAW_TEXT (glossary ) writes mapped, normalized, unescaped text (HTML script and style; SERE0008 for an unencodable character). Character maps now apply to every method but adaptive and the canonical forms (section 12).

HTML is a mode of the XML node writer in src/serialize_xml.c (is_html, with has_html_rules for what XHTML and HTML share); src/serialize_html.c holds what HTML adds: void and HTML 4 empty elements (one table, also used by XHTML), boolean attributes (the HTML 4.01 and HTML5 lists), raw text elements, processing instructions (<?t d> before HTML5, SERE0015 for ">"; <!--?t d?--> with HTML5). Requested version: html-version, else version, else 5.0. No-namespace elements are HTML elements (unknown names inline, as span); with HTML5 also XHTML-namespace ones (unprefixed, prefix normalization of ); others are XML islands. Doctype <!DOCTYPE html ...>. SERE0014 for controls before HTML5.

Text and CSV (src/serialize_text.c): text writes the string value of the result tree with escape style NONE. CSV takes a map (rows, columns) or a sequence of arrays; members atomize (one-member arrays unwrapped, nodes by string value), else SERE0025; a field is quoted when it, or a replacement of one of its mapped characters, holds the separator, the quote or a line end; separator equal to the quote or a line end is SEPM0016.

JSON (src/serialize_json.c): frames on a heap stack (); nodes by a sub-serialization (sxml_serializer_write_node_as_string, which calls only the XML and text methods, so no cycle); doubles by their xs:double cast text, NaN null, infinities 1e9999 (SERE0020 when canonical); canonical: keys sorted by UTF-16 units (heapsort), numbers as ECMAScript from the shortest digits; SERE0022 checked by sorting only when some key is not string-like; indentation off with json-lines.

SERE0006 (left by ): XML and XHTML with version 1.0 (the default) raise it for C0 controls in text and attributes; 1.1 writes references. SERE0003 for comments with "--" or a final "-" and PIs with "?>" (XML, XHTML). A character map may map any XML 1.1 Char (U+0001 included; serialize.h says XML 1.0's production, already writes the 1.1 repertoire).

Parameter reader (src/serialize_parameters.c): both forms decode each parameter into one value and assign it the same way. Two arenas: a read fills the spare one and swaps on success. Map: unknown string keys are XPTY0004 (F&O 4.0 option conventions, QT4 serialize-xml-107-40, deviating from serialize.h's "ignored"), a QName key in no namespace XPTY0004, in a namespace ignored; nodes atomize for character map values. Document: unknown output:* children, attributes other than value (character-map: character, map-string), non-whitespace text and children in no namespace are SEPM0017; two children with one name SEPM0019; element lists use the default namespace (the spec's example), method names do not. fn:serialize (src/function_library_serialize.c) skips the encoding phase: UTF-16 is written as UTF-8, ISO-8859-1 bytes decoded, no byte order mark.
Not done: SERE0005 (names of the XML version), the text of nodes inside the JSON method beyond the four node methods, records omitting empty entries in JSON (no record marker on maps).
